9 Database catalogue
The following table names and columns are proposed implementation data. Registered records retain both UUID and readable prefixed identity under D39. Sections 9 and 22 must be read together: Section 22 adds the shared identity/control requirements omitted from the abbreviated table catalogue and diagrams. UUID primary/foreign keys, exact readable prefixes and physical schema details remain pending schema review. TIMESTAMPTZ is used for events and DATE for DOB; user-visible dates use DD-MMM-YYYY. Retention remains an explicit policy decision.

Uniqueness and matching
The requested composite key is Father Name + Nationality + National ID Type + ID Number. SYS_EMP_ID remains the canonical business identifier used in employee relationships. Apply the approved scope to both uniqueness constraints; the scope decision must be settled before a production migration.
Create the composite fingerprint using a keyed digest of a canonical, unambiguously encoded tuple. Use encryption for identifier recovery and a separate protected key reference for fingerprint generation. Do not use an ordinary unsalted hash of a low-entropy identifier. Version normalisation and fingerprint logic; key rotation requires a controlled dual-check/backfill transition.
A spelling change in father name could allow the same national ID under a different composite key. An additional same-nationality/type/ID duplicate-review check is proposed, not an approved replacement for the requested key. Identifier normalisation, issuer-country requirements and treatment of people without national ID remain pending business decisions.
Transactions and deletion
On execution, lock/claim the approved request; verify actor authority, config and identity constraints; allocate an Auto ID when needed; insert identity and responses; write request_result, audit and outbox; commit once. A unique constraint resolves simultaneous duplicate submissions. Do not allocate by MAX(id)+1. Sequence gaps may occur; gapless numbering is not promised.
Use RESTRICT for referenced master deletion; retire definitions or deactivate operational access through controlled requests. Do not cascade-delete employee history, approvals or audit. An actual erasure/retention policy requires separate approved handling.

Unexpected server failures return a safe 500 with correlation reference. Apply request-size limits and pagination limits from approved configuration.
A browser may not select a database table, executable function or raw SQL. The API resolves the registered component+operation mapping. Authentication is server-side; entity/record/field authorisation is enforced on every read and write. Administrative approvals are never accepted from client-supplied actor or timestamp fields.

HRMS-specific code retains EMP: COSEMPManagementModule in cos-emp-management.module.ts belongs to Employee Management. COSEMPRegHandler in cos-emp-reg.handler.ts belongs to Employee Registration. COSEMPRegForm in cos-emp-reg-form.tsx is the frontend registration component. COSEMPRegRequestDTO in cos-emp-reg-request.dto.ts is the employee-specific payload; COSCommonRequestDTO in cos-common-request.dto.ts is the reusable envelope. A technical module class does not create a new architecture module or require one backend module per registration component.
For Bulk Upload, COSBulkUploadService reads and maps source rows, then delegates employee business checks to COSEMPRegHandler. Google Sheet Sync similarly uses COSSheetSyncService for authorised source access and delegates domain checks. Both submit through COSRequestService and the governed approval/execution path. Shared services must not depend on employee-specific DTOs or employee database tables; registered contracts and handlers provide the boundary.
Naming and coding controls
Registered custom functions use COS_ACTION_OBJECT. Classes, services, DTOs and schemas use COS + PascalCase. Source files use cos-<scope>-<purpose>.<role>.ts or cos-<scope>-<purpose>.tsx. API routes use /api/v1/cos/<resource>. JSON fields, parameters and local variables use lower_snake_case. Preserve framework-required exports and third-party names. EMP_Reg and SYS_EMP_ID are retained. Master output names have no RPT suffix. The agreed conventions apply to this design; global publication and installed-code migrations remain separate.
Each service/API/DTO/function/file records an owner reference, role, version and implementation status. Resolve architectural ancestry from the owner instead of manually maintaining inconsistent suite/engine/module paths on every artefact. Controllers handle transport; DTOs define contracts; services/handlers implement business behaviour; repositories perform scoped transactional data access. No arbitrary client-selected tables, SQL or executable function paths. Reuse validation, access, approval, audit and idempotency infrastructure.
Visuals, examples and generation
Diagram_Register identifies diagram type, scope, source registers, layout profile and asset reference. Asset_Register records the seven existing native embedded image object references against this document; standalone Drive asset IDs remain blank because extraction has not occurred. Architecture/DB diagrams derive from registered objects, tables and relations. Screen mockups derive from registered layouts and controls. Actual screenshots require a running application and capture/build provenance; none are claimed here.
Example_Register stores illustrative scenario, inputs, expected output, explanation and classification separately from actual records. Document_Section_Register stores versioned narrative and section ordering. Design_Table_Register preserves native table headers and rows as versioned source snapshots. Typed design records take precedence for reviewed canonical definitions; conflicting legacy snapshots require reconciliation and must not be silently mixed into a current output. Output_Profile_Register defines Full Design, All Standards, Selected Standards, Developer Guide, AI Working Standard and Database Design views.
The proposed generation service resolves scope and approved effective versions, applies dependencies and approved exceptions, validates references, freezes a source manifest, renders diagrams/mockups, retrieves permitted assets, creates native tables and sections, updates the permanent target with the required backup, verifies output and records the run. Generation_Run_Register is intentionally empty until an actual generation occurs. A registered command such as follow coding standard is a lookup specification; it does not install an AI connector or enforce other chats.
Remaining work and version control
Pending items include full rule completion for all 20 standards, source consolidation, permanent UUID/readable-ID allocation, shared engine placement, field semantics, named owners, ID/uniqueness scope, technology/repository selection, source/sync policy, separate visual assets and asset folders, bulk/sync mockup rendering, actual code and tests, command retrieval, generation services, retention/recovery targets and publication. Keep unknown provider IDs and approval identities blank. No runtime services, sync jobs, database migrations or published releases are created by registering the design.
